### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/api/wire-format.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via HonoHttpServer (symbol, a top-level class))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **9** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 658d84f5756e616d6418cb0ecf38630e04b4e341` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `edf77727516c530e813ee26b289d218d6243ba83` — the merge of head `586338ffbdd25e1fa9c86965dcfa3534e8993ad0` into base `658d84f5756e616d6418cb0ecf38630e04b4e341`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin edf77727516c530e813ee26b289d218d6243ba83 && git checkout edf77727516c530e813ee26b289d218d6243ba83
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 658d84f5756e616d6418cb0ecf38630e04b4e341 586338ffbdd25e1fa9c86965dcfa3534e8993ad0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 658d84f5756e616d6418cb0ecf38630e04b4e341 && git merge --no-ff 586338ffbdd25e1fa9c86965dcfa3534e8993ad0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 658d84f5756e616d6418cb0ecf38630e04b4e341
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 658d84f5756e616d6418cb0ecf38630e04b4e341` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `586338ffbdd25e1fa9c86965dcfa3534e8993ad0`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

_Sections ① to ③ are the round-1 review of the earlier head `2ff6bb0735`, kept as the record of what round 2 had to answer. Its verdict on that head was FAIL (M1, M2 must-fix; S1, S2 should-fix). The Round 2 delta after ③ judges the head named above, and its verdict is the one this record gives._

Read against `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at head `2ff6bb0735` (net diff over `origin/main` `620b6e6d40`, nine files, +176/−9), card #30920 (body, triage 6684701060, claim 6708147577, dev report 6710121990) and PR #31189's body. Node semantics are read from the Node `v22.11.0` sources `lib/_http_server.js` and `lib/_http_outgoing.js` (`.nvmrc` is `22`). Served tier: the file list holds no published schema and no governed path, and the changeset's `Clause-②: no` carries no `(narrowing)` arm, so the record tool decides the declaration face.

**Gates on this head (the check-runs are the verdicts).** Green: `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` lane, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`. Still `in_progress` when this was read: `Test Core` 1/8–8/8, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` 1/16–16/16, `Build & E2E UI`. `Lint UI` skipped. So `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` have no verdict on this head yet. That is not green.

#### The drain fix (`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts`)

- **`Connection: close` on responses whose headers are not yet written (HTTP/1.1, TLS): correct.** `_storeHeader` decides the connection header from `shouldKeepAlive` at the moment `_header` is built, and `headersSent` is `!!_header`. So the `close()` loop's `!res.headersSent` check matches that decision point, with no partial state. A response whose header went out `close` sets `_last`, and `resOnFinish` then calls `socket.destroySoon()` after the flush. That is Node's own close-after-response path. The request-time branch runs in a `prependListener('request')`, ahead of `@hono/node-server`'s listener, so even a synchronous response cannot write its headers first. `close()` runs in a later macrotask, so it cannot interleave with a header write. TLS uses the same `_http_server` path, since `https.Server` carries the connection tracking and `closeIdleConnections()`. **HTTP/2 is not served:** both arms of `tryListen` build an `http`/`https` HTTP/1.1 server, and none is `node:http2`.
- **⛔ M1 — the `closeIdleConnections()` arm can cut another connection's response short.** Node 22 skips an idle connection only `if (socket._httpMessage && !socket._httpMessage.finished)` (`_http_server.js` 594–608). `OutgoingMessage.end()` sets `finished = true` at once (`_http_outgoing.js` 1146). `'finish'`, and with it `detachSocket`, comes only after the last write is flushed (`onFinish`, `resOnFinish` 1000–1002). A GET's connection is on the idle list as soon as its request has been parsed. So a connection B whose response has called `end()` but is still flushing counts as idle and not skippable: for example, a large JSON body handed to `end()` in one call, going to a slow client. `trackForDrain` calls the server-wide `closeIdleConnections()` every time any keep-alive response A ends during the drain, and that call `socket.destroy()`s B mid-body. Before this PR the same Node call ran only at the single instant the drain began. Now it runs again each time an A ends, for the whole window. The likely A is a stream or SSE response whose headers went out before `close()`. So the fix trades a keep-alive wait for a truncated response on a concurrent connection. Three claims are false in this case: the JSDoc's "That call skips any socket still writing a response", the changeset's "In-flight requests still complete and are never cut short" (it ships in `CHANGELOG.md`), and the body's matching sentence. **Fix:** release only the ending response's own socket. Once `res` has closed, `socket` is flushed and detached, so if the drain is on and `socket` is still open with no `_httpMessage` assigned, `socket.destroySoon()` (or `end()`) it. Never call the server-wide sweep from there. Correct the JSDoc, the changeset and the body. Add a pin: during a drain, a response already `end()`-ed to a client that is not reading arrives complete (byte count equals its `Content-Length`) while another keep-alive stream ends.
- **⛔ M2 — `inFlightResponses` leaks pipelined responses, on the hot path.** The prepended listener adds every response to a strong `Set` and removes it only on the response's `'close'`. A `ServerResponse` emits `'close'` only through `resOnFinish`, which needs `'finish'` and so a socket, or through `onServerResponseClose`, which fires for `socket._httpMessage` alone (`_http_server.js` 257–297, 796–808, 1026–1030). A pipelined request parsed while the one before it is pending gets a response queued in `state.outgoing`, with `res.socket === null`. If the socket then dies, that queued response is never assigned and never emits `'close'`. It stays in the `Set` with its `req` and any body the handler buffered into `outputData`, until `close()` clears the set. Any unauthenticated client can pipeline requests and drop the socket, over and over: unbounded memory growth on every request path of a long-running server. Before this PR nothing kept those objects alive past their socket. **Fix:** tie each entry's life to its socket's life as well as its response's: remove it on the socket's `'close'`, or track per connection. Pin it: pipeline N requests behind a pending one, destroy the socket, and assert the tracking set returns to empty.
- **Force-close: unchanged.** The `closeAllConnections()` timer block is byte-identical. The new lines only set the flag before it and clear state after it. A late `'close'` after the window finds `draining === false`, or a destroyed socket, and does nothing.
- **Outside a drain:** the per-request behaviour is unchanged, because the `'close'` handler returns at `!this.draining`. The per-request work is an extra listener, a `Set` add/delete and a closure: a small cost I would accept. The `Set` is not acceptable as it stands, because of M2.
- **Ablation honesty.** Both arms the PR names were ablated, with red readings recorded in the body: `expected 'keep-alive' to be 'close'` and `expected 3006 to be less than 1000`. Reading the cases, each fails without its half: the in-flight case reaches the `close()` loop, and the streamed case reaches the `closeIdleConnections()` arm. **S1:** the request-time branch `if (this.draining) res.shouldKeepAlive = false` has no case. A request whose headers complete after `close()` began goes through it: one mid-headers at drain start, which is active and so not idle, or a pipelined one. Every case stays green with that line deleted. Pin it with a raw socket: write half the request headers, call `close()`, write the rest, and assert `Connection: close`.

#### Test-side changes

- **`metadata-protocol` derivation: not weaker.** The removed `flatten(a)` vs `flatten(b)` compared two back-to-back calls in one process state. The kept comparison, the derivation now vs the module-load singleton, spans the wider gap in time and state that the case's comment says it guards. A nondeterministic or state-dependent derivation that the a/b pair would catch also differs from the singleton. The added `expect(a).not.toBe(REFERENCE_SITES)` closes a hole the old form had: a memoised `deriveReferenceSites()` returned `a === b === singleton` and passed vacuously. `deriveReferenceSites()` builds a fresh index each call (`reference-sites.ts:630`, singleton at `:729`).
- **`client` shared server at file load: no new shared state.** The cases already shared one `fileServer()`. Only who pays for building it moved: from the first case's clock to collection. The warm-up's engine is destroyed by `closeEngines()` before the new build. The new engine joins `engines` and is destroyed by `afterAll(closeEngines)`. Every case still signs up its own user through its own client. Pin ④ still holds: one column-0 `await signedIn();`, one `beforeEach`, no `}, NUMBER);`.
- **Timeouts.** The budgets follow the rule in `share-link-password-webcontainer.test.ts`: 3x the slowest `Test Core` reading, rounded up to the next second, with readings and arithmetic at the case. The numbers check out: 3×2629→8000, 3×2499→8000, 3×2949→9000, 3×2605→8000. None is a global raise, a skip or a retry. No comment line opens with `test-budget:`, so `readTestBudget` sees no stray declaration. `plugin-security`'s file-level `test-budget: 20` header is untouched. Note: that rule applies to readings over half the default, and `driver-sql`'s 2499 ms is 1 ms under that line. The card asked for a budget anyway, and the budget is harmless, but the comment's "The rule is 3x the slowest reading" drops the threshold.
- **`cli` unmanaged-tables left unchanged: justified.** The case body is synchronous assertions over `stack`. The boot is in `beforeEach` under its own `180_000`. vitest's `testTimeout` wraps only the body, while the reported duration includes the hooks. So the 5 s default cannot red this case, and a per-case timeout would bind nothing. The `bootSchemaStack` cost inside a clocked hook predates this PR. The dev recorded it as an out-of-scope observation.

#### Seat's choice: client cut only, no timeout. **Agree.**

The file header says a recurrence is answered "by cutting the case's own work, ⛔ not a timeout". Pin ④ enforces the literal form. A named-constant budget would slip past pin ④'s `[\d_]+` regex while breaking the recorded rule, so "no timeout" is the only reading consistent with the file. The cut is real: server and better-auth construction moved out of ①'s clock, 729–800 → 558–583 ms locally. If CI reds it, the lever is the probe's own work, as the header says.

#### Landing

- `Fixes #30920`: present.
- Body vs tree: the body names the nine files the tree carries. Its table and readings match the code comments. It repeats M1's false "skips any socket still writing a response" claim, which must be corrected with the code.
- Governed: no. None of the nine paths is a register row. 185 changed lines, under 3,000. The owning seat lands it through the queue after ACCEPT and a fully green head.
- Changeset: present, `'@objectstack/plugin-hono-server': patch`, with both declaration lines. The six test-only packages publish nothing. Its prose must drop or narrow "never cut short" (M1).

**Must-fix (FAIL):**
- **M1:** the server-wide `closeIdleConnections()` in the `'close'` arm can destroy a concurrent connection whose response is ended but still flushing, so a response is truncated. Release only the ending response's own socket, correct the JSDoc, changeset and body claims, and add the slow-reader pin.
- **M2:** `inFlightResponses` never drops a queued pipelined response whose socket dies, so memory grows without bound on the request hot path and any client can trigger it. Tie entries to the socket's life and add the pipelined-then-destroyed pin.

**Should-fix:**
- **S1:** pin the request-time `shouldKeepAlive = false` branch (raw-socket case, request headers completing after `close()`).
- **S2:** in the `driver-sql` budget comment, state the rule with its over-half threshold, or say why a 2499 ms reading takes a budget anyway.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`: correct. `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and `none` takes `patch`. The change alters shutdown timing and connection headers during a drain, and nothing a metadata author writes. No other package publishes a change. The level stands after M1 and M2 are fixed. Only the changeset's prose changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Published package: `plugin-hono-server` ships the drain path and the per-request listener. Both must-fixes sit in shipped code.
- Hot path: the per-request listener is new on every HTTP request (M2).
- Spec, ADR-0087 and governed surfaces: untouched. Not Tier H or Tier S. Under the size line.
- Gates: `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` were still running on this head. ⛔ Do not arm until both conclude `success`, on a head carrying M1 and M2.

### Round 2 delta — head `586338ffbd`

Read: `git diff 2ff6bb0735..586338ffbd` (four files, +207/−21: `adapter.ts`, `adapter-drain.test.ts`, the `driver-sql` budget comment and the changeset), dev delta report 6710694928, and the PR body as the seat patched it. Node semantics are from the `v22.11.0` sources `lib/_http_server.js`, `lib/_http_outgoing.js` and `lib/net.js`. Nothing was built, run or checked out.

**M1: fixed.** The `'close'` arm no longer touches the server. It calls `socket.destroySoon()` on the ending response's own connection, and only under four conditions:
- the drain is on;
- no other response that connection owes is still pending (`owed.size === 0`);
- `res.writableFinished` is true;
- the socket is neither destroyed nor ended.

The server-wide `closeIdleConnections()` survives only at drain start, unchanged from `main`. The checks against Node 22 hold:
- **When the arm runs.** A response's `'close'` comes from `emitCloseNT`, queued by `resOnFinish`. That runs on `'finish'`, which `onFinish` emits from the last write's callback, after `detachSocket`. Or it comes from `onServerResponseClose` when the socket dies, and the `socket.destroyed` guard returns in that case.
- **`writableFinished` is true by then.** Its getter (`_http_outgoing.js` 175–183) is `finished && outputSize === 0 && (!socket || socket.writableLength === 0)`. Once the response is detached, it reads true.
- **Every byte is flushed before the close.** `Socket.prototype.destroySoon` (`net.js` 788–796) calls `end()`. That queues FIN behind every pending write and calls `destroy` only on the socket's own `'finish'`. Nothing queued is dropped. TLS sockets inherit the same method.
- **"Nothing else pending" is correct under pipelining.** Every parsed request adds its response to its connection's set in the prepended `'request'` listener, including responses queued with no socket yet. `resOnFinish` assigns the next queued response synchronously, before `emitCloseNT` runs on the next tick. So a pending pipelined response always keeps `owed.size` above 0, and the connection is left for that response's own arm, or for Node's `_last` close when its header went out `close`. A request whose bytes arrive after the release meets a FIN or a reset. That is the ordinary keep-alive close race, the same one `closeIdleConnections()` has, and no worse.
- **The claims now match the code.** The JSDoc carries the ⛔ against a sweep, the changeset reads "closes its own connection once every byte of it has been flushed. Other connections are not touched", and the body says the same. "Never cut short" is gone everywhere.

**M2: fixed.** The bookkeeping is a `Map` from each connection to a `Set` of the responses it owes, keyed by `req.socket`, which is set even for a queued pipelined response. Each entry is dropped on the socket's own `'close'`, through one `once` listener per connection, so there is no per-request socket listener and no MaxListeners risk. An entry can only live while its socket lives, and so does the socket's own memory.
- **No leak from a connection that never closes.** A socket that never emits `'close'` is an open connection. It already holds that memory itself, and Node's `keepAliveTimeout`, `headersTimeout` and `requestTimeout` bound it.
- **The drain bounds it too.** `close()` force-closes every connection when the window ends, then `inFlightResponses.clear()`.
- **No stale cross-reference.** The `=== created` guard keeps a stale listener from deleting a newer entry.
- **The queued responses are collectable.** After the entry is dropped, they are referenced only by their own `'close'` closures.

**The new pins test what they claim.**
- **Slow reader (M1).** B's 32 MiB response goes to a paused raw socket. It is released after `close()` starts, so the drain-start sweep cannot reach it. The case asserts the premise outright: `writableEnded === true` and `writableFinished === false`. So it cannot pass with B already flushed. Then A's keep-alive stream ends, and the case asserts the byte count against `Content-Length`. Ablated to the round-1 sweep it is red, and the dev reports `expected 3919730 to be 33554432`.
- **Pipelined then destroyed (M2).** Four requests go in one write. The case asserts 4 tracked, destroys the socket, and asserts 0. The ablation that removes the drop on connection close reads `expected 3 to be +0`. The helper reads the private field by name. That is accepted coupling for a bookkeeping pin.
- **Late headers (S1).** Half the request headers are written, then `close()`, then the rest. The parser has begun the message, so the connection is active and the drain-start sweep skips it. The response is created after `close()`'s loop has run, so only the request-time line can flip it, and the ablation reads `expected keep-alive to be close`. It goes red on the assertion, not by hanging: the round-2 own-connection arm still ends the connection.

**S2: done.** The `driver-sql` comment states the over-half threshold, says 2499 ms sits 1 ms under it, and gives the reason it keeps the budget.

**The pre-existing hole: outside this PR, unchanged from `main`. File it as its own card.** A response that has called `end()` but is still flushing at the instant `close()` starts is destroyed mid-body. On `main`, `close()` already calls `server.close()`, which in Node 22 runs `httpServerPreClose` and so `closeIdleConnections()` (`_http_server.js` 526–529, 573). It then calls `closeIdleConnections()` again itself. Both use the same `finished` test that counts an ended-but-flushing response as done. Round 2 adds no call at that instant. Its `Connection: close` flip touches only responses whose headers are unwritten, and an ended response's headers are always written. So exposure at drain start is identical to `main`. Round 1 had widened it to every response end in the window; round 2 narrows it back to that single instant. It is a reproducible defect: the dev's reordered slow-reader case reads `expected 3919702 to be 33554432` on this branch. Prime Directive #10 owes it a card, for the seat to file. The dev reported it, and the PR body names it under "Found, not fixed here". It does not block this PR.

**Nit (no finding).** The `type OwedResponses` alias and the `node:net` type import sit between import statements, above `./route-pattern`. `Lint · ESLint` is green on this head, so this is style only.

**Landing on `586338ffbd`.**
- `Fixes #30920`: present.
- The body matches the tree.
- No governed surface.
- 371 changed lines, under 3,000.
- `patch` changeset, unchanged in level.

**Check-runs on `586338ffbd`, as read.** Green:
- `TypeScript Type Check` and all four `Type Check ·` lanes
- `Lint & Repo Gates` and every `Lint ·` lane
- `Build Core`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Live E2E UI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`
- `Test Core` 5/8 and 8/8
- 9 of 16 `Test UI` shards

Still `in_progress`:
- `Test Core` 1–4/8, 6/8, 7/8
- `Type Check UI`
- seven `Test UI` shards
- a second `Check Changeset` run (one run is already `success`)

`Lint UI` was skipped. The required `Test Core` has no verdict yet. ⛔ Do not arm until every required context concludes `success` on this head.

**Round 2: no must-fix, no should-fix remains.** The verdict below is on the code at head `586338ffbdd25e1fa9c86965dcfa3534e8993ad0`. Landing still waits on that head's required check-runs.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-30920-test-core-slow-cases`
Reviewed-by: `session_017ihL2ebbZkr2QAEG1x7UC8`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：
  - Hono 服务器优雅关闭时，正在处理的请求一结束就只关它自己的连接：还没发响应头的，回 `Connection: close`；已发 keep-alive 头的，等全部字节发完再关。
  - 关闭期间的连接记账改成按连接存放，连接一断就清掉。
  - 另外 7 条慢测试用例：2 条砍掉重复工作，4 条按“CI 最慢读数 ×3”给了单独超时，1 条经测量不需要改。
- 为什么改：Test Core 有 9 条用例贴着 vitest 默认的 5 秒超时。其中两条关闭用例要等 3.2 到 4.2 秒，原因是空闲的 keep-alive 连接要等客户端先断开。改完后约 0.2 秒。
- 风险与回滚：
  - 生产代码只动 `plugin-hono-server` 的关闭路径。
  - 第一轮审查发现两处缺陷（会截断别的连接上还在发送的大响应；流水线请求断连后会被一直留在内存里），第二轮都已修好，并各有专门用例钉住。
  - 关闭“开始那一刻”仍可能截断已结束但还在发送的响应，这是 main 上原有的问题，本 PR 不改变它，已另立卡 #31208。
  - 回滚：revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/adapter.ts` 的 `trackForDrain`、`responsesOwedOn` 和 `close()`，以及 `adapter-drain.test.ts` 新增的三条用例。
- 两分钟验证：运行 `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-hono-server exec vitest run src/adapter-drain.test.ts src/adapter-tls-listener.test.ts`，应看到 12 条全过，两条关闭用例约 0.2 秒。
